>                             ],
>                             "articles": [
>                                 {
>                                     "title": "Deep learning",
>                                     "url": "https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=WLN3QrAAAAAJ&pagesize=100&citation_for_view=WLN3QrAAAAAJ:lo0OIn9KAZgC",
>                                     "publication_year": "2015",
>                                     "total_citations": 122610,
>                                     "authors": ["Y LeCun", "Y Bengio", "G Hinton"],
>                                     "all_authors": true,
>                                     "publication": "nature 521 (7553), 436-444"
>                                 }
>                             ],
>                             "co_authors": [
>                                 {
>                                     "id": "kukA0LcAAAAJ",
>                                     "profile_url": "https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=kukA0LcAAAAJ",
>                                     "name": "Yoshua Bengio",
>                                     "designation": "Professor of computer science, University of Montreal, Mila, IVADO, CIFAR",
>                                     "thumbnail": "https://scholar.googleusercontent.com/citations?view_op=view_photo&user=kukA0LcAAAAJ&citpid=3"
>                                 }
>                             ],
>                             "metadata": { "last_scraped_source": "2026-09-09T07:39:01.451002Z" }
>                         }
>                     ]
>                 }
>             }
>         ]
>     }
> ]
> ```
>
> > [!NOTE]
> >
> > The response above is trimmed. The live call returned 799 articles, 117
> > co-authors, and 19 timeseries points, and `social_handles` is left out.
>
> The full section is large. It averages about 26 KB per person and can reach
> about 1 MB, because `articles` and `co_authors` list everything. When you do not
> need the publication list, request only the sub-fields you read. This call
> returns the name, the profile URL, and the lifetime h-index on their own:
>
> ```bash Request theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
> curl --request POST \
>   --url https://api.crustdata.com/person/enrich \
>   --header 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
>   --header 'content-type: application/json' \
>   --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01' \
>   --data '{
>     "professional_network_profile_urls": ["https://www.linkedin.com/in/yann-lecun/"],
>     "fields": ["basic_profile.name", "research_profiles.name", "research_profiles.profile_url", "research_profiles.h_index.all"]
>   }'
> ```
>
> ```json Response (trimmed) theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
> {
>     "crustdata_person_id": 1284112,
>     "basic_profile": { "name": "Yann LeCun" },
>     "research_profiles": [
>         {
>             "name": "Yann LeCun",
>             "profile_url": "https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=WLN3QrAAAAAJ",
>             "h_index": { "all": 175 }
>         }
>     ]
> }
> ```
>
> > [!NOTE]
> >
> > **Access and pricing.** `research_profiles` is enabled per account on API
> > version `2025-11-01`. Contact Crustdata to turn it on. The add-on costs
> > **2** credits per person returned with at least one research profile, on
> > top of the base enrich pricing. A person with no matched profile is not
> > charged the add-on. To filter and sort people by citation metrics, use the
> > `research_profiles.*` fields on
> > [Person Search](/person-docs/search/reference#research-profiles).

> **Certifications and honors (gated — needs field permission)**
>
> `certifications` and `honors` require field-level permission on your API key.
> Without it, the request returns a permission error — contact Crustdata to enable
> them for your key.
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
> curl --request POST \
>   --url https://api.crustdata.com/person/enrich \
>   --header 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
>   --header 'content-type: application/json' \
>   --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01' \
>   --data '{
>     "professional_network_profile_urls": ["https://www.linkedin.com/in/dvdhsu/"],
>     "fields": ["basic_profile", "certifications", "honors"]
>   }'
> ```

### More recipes

> **Handle no-match results**
>
> Not every identifier will resolve to a person. When there is no match, the
> `matches` array is empty.
>
> ```bash Request theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
> curl --request POST \
>   --url https://api.crustdata.com/person/enrich \
>   --header 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
>   --header 'content-type: application/json' \
>   --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01' \
>   --data '{
>     "professional_network_profile_urls": [
>       "https://www.linkedin.com/in/no-such-profile/"
>     ]
>   }'
> ```
>
> ```json Response theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
> [
>     {
>         "matched_on": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/no-such-profile/",
>         "match_type": "professional_network_profile_url",
>         "matches": []
>     }
> ]
> ```
>
> You still get a response entry for the identifier — `matched_on` tells you
> which input had no match. This makes it easy to track which lookups
> succeeded and which need a different approach.

> **Batch enrichment — look up multiple people at once**
>
> You can enrich up to **25 identifiers** in a single request. The response
> returns one entry per identifier, in the same order you submitted them.
>
> ```bash Request theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
> curl --request POST \
>   --url https://api.crustdata.com/person/enrich \
>   --header 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
>   --header 'content-type: application/json' \
>   --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01' \
>   --data '{
>     "professional_network_profile_urls": [
>       "https://www.linkedin.com/in/dvdhsu/",
>       "https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhilashchowdhary/"
>     ]
>   }'
> ```
>
> ```json Response theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
> [
>     {
>         "matched_on": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/dvdhsu/",
>         "match_type": "professional_network_profile_url",
>         "matches": [
>             {
>                 "confidence_score": 1.0,
>                 "person_data": {
>                     "basic_profile": {
>                         "name": "David Hsu",
>                         "headline": "Founder, CEO @ Retool",
>                         "current_title": "Founder, CEO",
>                         "location": {
>                             "city": "San Francisco",
>                             "state": "California",
>                             "country": "United States",
>                             "continent": "North America",
>                             "raw": "San Francisco Bay Area"
>                         }
>                     },
>                     "social_handles": {
>                         "professional_network_identifier": {
>                             "profile_url": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/dvdhsu"
>                         }
>                     }
>                 }
>             }
>         ]
>     },
>     {
>         "matched_on": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhilashchowdhary/",
>         "match_type": "professional_network_profile_url",
>         "matches": [
>             {
>                 "confidence_score": 1.0,
>                 "person_data": {
>                     "basic_profile": {
>                         "name": "Abhilash Chowdhary",
>                         "headline": "Co-founder at Crustdata (YC F24) | Real-time B2B data for AI agents",
>                         "current_title": "Co-Founder & CEO",
>                         "location": {
>                             "city": "San Francisco",
>                             "state": "California",
>                             "country": "United States of America",
>                             "continent": "North America",
>                             "raw": "San Francisco, California, United States"
>                         }
>                     },
>                     "social_handles": {
>                         "professional_network_identifier": {
>                             "profile_url": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhilashchowdhary"
>                         }
>                     }
>                 }
>             }
>         ]
>     }
> ]
> ```
>
> > [!NOTE]
> >
> > Response trimmed for clarity.
>
> **Batch enrichment tips**
>
> * The maximum batch size is **25 identifiers** per request.
> * Each entry in the response corresponds to the input at the same position, so you can match results back to your input list by index.
> * If some identifiers fail to match, their `matches` array will be empty, but the request still succeeds for the others.

> **Workflow — Search then Enrich**
>
> The most powerful pattern combines [Person Search](/person-docs/search/introduction) with
> Person Enrich. Search finds people matching your criteria; Enrich gets the
> full profile for each match.
>
> **Step 1:** Search for decision-makers at a target company.
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
> curl --request POST \
>   --url https://api.crustdata.com/person/search \
>   --header 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
>   --header 'content-type: application/json' \
>   --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01' \
>   --data '{
>     "filters": {
>       "op": "and",
>       "conditions": [
>         {
>           "field": "experience.employment_details.current.company_name",
>           "type": "in",
>           "value": ["Retool"]
>         },
>         {
>           "op": "or",
>           "conditions": [
>             { "field": "experience.employment_details.current.title", "type": "(.)", "value": "VP" },
>             { "field": "experience.employment_details.current.title", "type": "(.)", "value": "Director" },
>             { "field": "experience.employment_details.current.title", "type": "(.)", "value": "Head of" }
>           ]
>         }
>       ]
>     },
>     "limit": 5
>   }'
> ```
>
> **Step 2:** Take the profile URLs from the search results and enrich them
> for full profiles.
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
> curl --request POST \
>   --url https://api.crustdata.com/person/enrich \
>   --header 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
>   --header 'content-type: application/json' \
>   --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01' \
>   --data '{
>     "professional_network_profile_urls": [
>       "https://www.linkedin.com/in/dvdhsu/",
>       "https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhilashchowdhary/"
>     ]
>   }'
> ```
>
> This two-step pattern is the foundation for most sales, recruiting, and
> research workflows. Search narrows the universe; Enrich fills in the
> details.

***

## What to do next

* **Look up request/response details** — see [Enrich reference](/person-docs/enrichment/reference) for parameters, valid `fields` values, `person_data` sections, and errors.
* **Search first, then enrich** — use [Person Search](/person-docs/search/introduction) to find people by name, title, company, or location, then enrich the results.
* **Fetch fresh data from the web** — use [Person Live Enrich](/person-docs/enrichment/live-enrich) when cached enrich is not enough.


# Person Enrich reference
Source: https://docs.crustdata.com/person-docs/enrichment/reference

Reference for Person Enrich: request parameters, response fields, fields parameter, person_data sections, and errors.

Reference material for [Person Enrich](/person-docs/enrichment/introduction): request
parameters, response fields, valid `fields` values, `person_data` section
catalog, and errors.

For walk-through examples, see [Person Enrich](/person-docs/enrichment/introduction).

***

## Request parameter reference

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| `professional_network_profile_urls` | string\[] | Yes | — | Profile URLs to enrich. Max 25. |
| `fields` | string\[] | No | `basic_profile`, `social_handles` | Specific field paths or section groups to return. When omitted, only `basic_profile` and `social_handles` are returned. |
| `preview` | boolean | No | `false` | Enabled per account on request. Where enabled, the API returns a basic profile at 0 credits and ignores `fields`. You cannot combine it with `enrich_realtime`. Without the grant, the API returns `400 invalid_request`. See [Errors](#errors). |

Vanity URLs (`/in/dvdhsu`) and URN URLs (`/in/ACoAA...`, `/in/ACwAA...`) are
both accepted, and both match case-insensitively. `matched_on` echoes the
identifier exactly as you sent it.

***

## Response fields reference

Each item in the response array contains:

| Field | Type | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `matched_on` | string | The input profile URL |
| `match_type` | string | `professional_network_profile_url` |
| `match_status` | string | `matched`, `not_found`, or `redacted`. `redacted` means the person asked Crustdata to remove their data: `matches` stays empty, nothing is billed, and retrying or live enrich does not change it. `not_found` means the profile is not in the dataset yet. |
| `matches` | array | Array of candidate matches (may be empty for no-match) |
| `matches[].confidence_score` | number | 0 to 1. How confident the match is. `1.0` = exact match. |
| `matches[].person_data` | object | Full enriched profile. See [`person_data` sections](#person_data-sections) below. |

***

## Using the `fields` parameter

By default, the API returns only the `basic_profile` and `social_handles`
sections. Use the `fields` parameter to request the additional sections or
dot-paths you need.

```bash Request — specific fields theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.crustdata.com/person/enrich \
  --header 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01' \
  --data '{
    "professional_network_profile_urls": [
      "https://www.linkedin.com/in/dvdhsu/"
    ],
    "fields": [
      "basic_profile.summary",
      "dev_platform_profiles"
    ]
  }'
```

> [!TIP]
>
> Need email addresses or phone numbers? Use
> [Contact Enrich](/person-docs/contact/enrich).

### Popular fields for profile and developer workflows

| Field path | What it returns |
| - | - |
| `basic_profile.summary` | The person's summary or about text |
| `dev_platform_profiles` | Developer platform profiles when available |
| `social_handles.dev_platform_identifier.profile_url` | Canonical developer platform profile URL when available |
| `experience.employment_details.current.name` | The person's current company name |

### `person_data` sections

The `person_data` object contains the following sections. Pass any of these
names to `fields` to include that section, or use dot-paths like
`basic_profile.summary` to request a specific sub-field.

| Section | Key fields | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `crustdata_person_id` | integer | Top-level Crustdata identifier for the enriched profile |
| `updated_at` | date-time string (nullable) | Top-level timestamp of the most recent profile refresh |
| `basic_profile` | `name`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `headline`, `current_title`, `normalized_title` ([JTN](/guides/job-title-normalization), beta), `professional_network_name`, `summary`, `location`, `languages`, `last_updated`, `profile_picture_permalink` | Core identity and role |
| `professional_network` | `profile_picture_permalink`, `connections`, `followers`, `joined_date`, `verifications`, `open_to_cards`, `pronoun`, `location.raw`, `location.city`, `location.state`, `location.country`, `location.continent` | Profile metadata when available |
| `social_handles` | `professional_network_identifier.profile_url`, `professional_network_identifier.urn_url` (permanent URN-based URL; requires field-level permission on your API key), `dev_platform_identifier.profile_url`, `twitter_identifier.slug` | Available social identifiers |
| `experience` | `employment_details.current[]`, `employment_details.past[]` (each role includes `company_status`), `years_of_experience` (career total as a band, for example `More than 10 years`), `years_of_experience_raw` (number) | Full employment history and career totals |
| `education` | `schools[]` | Education background |
| `certifications` | `name`, `issuing_organization`, `issue_date`, `expiration_date` | Certifications. Requires field-level permission on your API key. |
| `honors` | `title`, `issuer`, `issued_date`, `description` | Honors and awards. Requires field-level permission on your API key. |
| `skills` | `professional_network_skills[]` | Professional skills |
| `dev_platform_profiles` | developer platform profile objects | Developer platform data when available |
| `social_posts` | list of post objects | Up to the 10 most recent posts the person authored, newest first (gated beta add-on; see [`social_posts` fields](#social_posts-fields)) |
| `assessment` | `authenticity.verdict`, `authenticity.tier` | Computed authenticity assessment of the profile (see [`assessment` fields](#assessment-fields)) |
| `research_profiles` | list of author profile objects | Matched academic author profiles, best match first (enabled on request; see [`research_profiles` fields](#research_profiles-fields)) |

### `assessment` fields

The `assessment` section carries a computed view of how well a profile stands
up to verification. It is never returned by default: request it explicitly via
`fields`, either as the whole group (`"fields": ["assessment"]`) or as a single
leaf such as `assessment.authenticity.verdict`.

`assessment` is returned only by `/person/enrich`, and it requires field-level
permission on your API key. Without the grant, naming it in `fields` returns
`403` with `Access denied to fields: assessment`. On `/person/search` both
paths are filterable and `tier` is sortable, but they are never returned in
search results: naming one in that endpoint's `fields` returns `400` with
`Invalid fields: assessment.authenticity.tier`. Sorting on
`assessment.authenticity.tier` ascending puts the most trusted profiles first.
For a worked request and response, see the
[Examples](/person-docs/enrichment/introduction#examples) on the introduction page.

| Field | Type | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `authenticity.verdict` | string (nullable) | One of `clearly_genuine`, `probably_genuine`, `cannot_verify`, `probably_fabricated`, `clearly_fabricated`. |
| `authenticity.tier` | integer (nullable) | Authenticity tier from 0 (most trusted) to 9 (least trusted). Sort ascending to put the most trusted first. |

Both paths are filterable on `/person/search`. `authenticity.verdict` takes the
five values above; an unrecognized value is not rejected, it simply matches
nothing. `authenticity.tier` accepts 0 through 9, and a filter for 10 matches
nothing.

Request a single leaf to get just that one, for example
`"fields": ["basic_profile.name", "assessment.authenticity.verdict"]` returns
`assessment.authenticity.verdict` on its own.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Read `cannot_verify` as thin evidence, not as fraud. It is the expected
> verdict for a sparse profile. Treat `probably_fabricated` as a flag for
> human review rather than a trigger for automated action, and do not use
> either verdict as the sole basis for a decision about a person.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Not a billed add-on.** Unlike `social_posts`, requesting `assessment`
> costs nothing extra. A person enrich for `["basic_profile.name"]` and one
> for `["basic_profile.name", "assessment"]` both report
> `x-credits-used: 1`.

> [!NOTE]
>
> `verdict` and `tier` are populated independently, so a profile can carry a
> `tier` with a null `verdict`. The two ends of the range behave differently:
> every tier 0 profile also carries `clearly_genuine`, while of the 25,434
> profiles at tier 9 only 11 carry any verdict at all. Read a null `verdict`
> as "not labelled", and prefer `tier` when you need a signal that is present
> on the untrusted end of the range.

***

### `social_posts` fields

The `social_posts` section returns posts the person authored. It is never
included by default; request it explicitly via `fields` (for example
`"fields": ["basic_profile", "social_posts"]`). Quote posts (reposts with
added commentary) are included; plain reshares of someone else's post are not.

Each entry in `social_posts` is one post, newest first, up to 10 per record:

| Field | Type | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `share_url` | string | Public URL of the post |
| `text` | string | Post text content |
| `date_posted` | date-time string | When the post was published |
| `post_type` | string | `original`, `repost_quote` (a repost with added commentary), or `repost_without_thoughts`. Plain reshares of someone else's post are not returned, so expect `original` and `repost_quote`. |
| `has_video` | boolean | True when the post contains a video |
| `hyperlinks` | object | URLs extracted from the post: `media_urls`, `other_urls`, `company_professional_network_urls`, `person_professional_network_urls` |
| `hashtags` | array of string | Hashtags used in the post |
| `engagement` | object | `total_reactions`, `total_comments`, `num_shares`, and `reactions_by_type` with per-type counts (`LIKE`, `PRAISE`, `APPRECIATION`, `EMPATHY`, `INTEREST`, `ENTERTAINMENT`) |

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Access and pricing.** `social_posts` is a beta add-on that requires
> field-level permission on your account and is available on API version
> `2025-11-01` only; without the grant the section is stripped from the
> response. Contact Crustdata to enable it. The add-on costs a flat **5**
> credits per profile on top of the base enrich pricing, however many posts
> come back, and returns at most 10. No posts returned means no add-on
> charge, and you are only billed when `social_posts` is in `fields`. To search posts across the network by
> keyword, use the
> [Social Post Search API](/social-post-docs/search/introduction).

### `research_profiles` fields

The `research_profiles` section carries the person's matched academic
author profiles. It is never returned by default: request it explicitly via
`fields`, either as the whole group (`"fields": ["research_profiles"]`) or as
sub-paths such as `research_profiles.h_index.all`. It is enabled per account.
Without the grant, naming it in `fields` returns `403` with
`Access denied to fields: research_profiles`. Contact Crustdata to turn it on.

The value is an array, best match first, because one person can hold more than
one author profile. A profile is linked only after a confident match, so
unmatched and under-review profiles never appear. When the person has no
matched profile, the key is absent from `person_data`. For a worked request and
response, see the
[Examples](/person-docs/enrichment/introduction#examples) on the introduction
page.

| Field | Type | Filled | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| `id` | string | 100% | Profile identifier, the `user` parameter of `profile_url`. |
| `profile_url` | string | 100% | URL of the author profile. |
| `name` | string | 100% | Name displayed on the profile. |
| `designation` | string | 100% | Free-text affiliation as displayed on the profile. |
| `affiliated_organisation` | string (nullable) | 62.4% | Organisation extracted from the affiliation. Can be an empty string. |
| `verified_email_domain` | string (nullable) | 99.99% | Institution domain verified for the profile. |
| `website` | string (nullable) | 36.9% | Homepage supplied on the profile. |
| `research_interests` | string\[] | 88.3% | Interest labels as listed on the profile. |
| `thumbnail` | string (nullable) | 71.4% | Profile picture URL. |
| `article_count` | integer | 100% | Number of publications on the profile. |
| `co_author_count` | integer | 100% | Number of linked co-authors. |
| `citations_count` | object | 100% | `all`, `recent`, and `recent_since_year`. `recent` counts from `recent_since_year` onwards. |
| `h_index` | object | 100% | Same three keys as `citations_count`. |
| `i10_index` | object | 100% | Same three keys as `citations_count`. |
| `citations_timeseries[]` | object\[] | 98.9% | `year` and `citations`, oldest year first. |
| `articles[]` | object\[] | 100% | Every publication: `title`, `url`, `publication_year` (string), `total_citations`, `authors[]`, `all_authors` (false when the source truncated the list), `publication`. |
| `co_authors[]` | object\[] | 49.0% | Every linked co-author: `id`, `profile_url`, `name`, `designation`, `thumbnail`. |
| `metadata.last_scraped_source` | date-time | 100% | When the profile was last refreshed from the web. |

Fill rates are the share of matched profiles that carry a value for the field.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Size.** The section averages about 26 KB per person and can reach about
> 1 MB, because `articles` and `co_authors` list everything. Request the
> sub-paths you read, for example
> `"fields": ["basic_profile.name", "research_profiles.h_index.all"]`, when
> you do not need the publication list.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Access and pricing.** `research_profiles` is enabled per account on API
> version `2025-11-01`. Contact Crustdata to turn it on. The add-on costs
> **2** credits per person returned with at least one research profile, on
> top of the base enrich pricing. A person with no matched profile is not
> charged the add-on. [Person Search](/person-docs/search/reference#research-profiles)
> can filter and sort on the same fields and returns a smaller copy of each
> profile.

***

## Fresh data and realtime enrichment

`/person/enrich` serves data from the cached dataset. When you need fresh
profile data retrieved in real time, use the dedicated
[Person Live Enrich](/person-docs/enrichment/live-enrich) endpoint
(`POST /person/professional_network/enrich/live`), which is designed for
real-time retrieval from the web.

> [!NOTE]
>
> If cached enrich is not enough, use
> [Person Live Enrich](/person-docs/enrichment/live-enrich) — it is
> designed for fresh profile retrieval from the web.

***

## Errors

| Status | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `400` | Invalid request: missing or wrong identifier type, malformed body, or `preview: true` on an account without preview. |
| `401` | Invalid or missing API key. |
| `403` | Permission denied or insufficient credits. |
| `500` | Internal server error. |

```json 400 — Bad request theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "error": {
        "type": "invalid_request",
        "message": "Exactly one identifier type must be provided.",
        "metadata": []
    }
}
```

```json 400 - Preview not enabled on the account theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "error": {
        "type": "invalid_request",
        "message": "Preview feature is not available for your account. Please reach out to Crustdata team.",
        "metadata": []
    }
}
```

```json 401 — Invalid API key theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "error": {
        "type": "unauthorized",
        "message": "Invalid API key in request.",
        "metadata": []
    }
}
```

```json 403 - Field not enabled on the account theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "error": {
        "type": "permission_error",
        "message": "Access denied to fields: research_profiles. To enable access, please book a call with us at https://meetings-na2.hubspot.com/chris-pisarski/web-demo-request",
        "metadata": [
            {
                "denied_fields": ["research_profiles"],
                "permitted_fields": ["basic_profile", "education", "experience"]
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

***

## API reference summary

| Detail | Value |
| - | - |
| **Endpoint** | `POST /person/enrich` |
| **Auth** | Bearer token + `x-api-version: 2025-11-01` |
| **Request** | `professional_network_profile_urls` (max 25). Optional: `fields`, `preview` (enabled per account on request). |
| **Response** | Top-level array: `[{ matched_on, match_type, match_status, matches: [{ confidence_score, person_data }] }]` |
| **No match** | `200` with empty `matches: []` for unmatched identifiers. |
| **Errors** | `400` (bad request), `401` (bad auth), `403` (permission/credits), `500` (server error) |

See the [full API reference](/openapi-specs/2025-11-01/introduction) for
the complete OpenAPI schema.


# Filter value enumeration
Source: https://docs.crustdata.com/person-docs/filter-values

Downloadable lists of the valid values for person search filter fields — skills, titles, regions, and employer industries.

Several person-search filter fields accept values from a fixed vocabulary. The
[autocomplete API](/person-docs/autocomplete/introduction) is always the current
source of truth, but these downloadable snapshots are convenient when you build
filters programmatically against a large set.

> [!WARNING]
>
> These files are point-in-time snapshots. For always-current values, use the
> [autocomplete API](/person-docs/autocomplete/introduction).

## Person filter values

| Field | Used by | Values | Download |
| - | - | - | - |
| `skills.professional_network_skills` | [Person Search](/person-docs/search/introduction) | 40,098 | [skills.json](https://s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/fulldocs.crustdata.com/examples/people-search/skills.json) |
| `CURRENT_TITLE` | [Person Live Search](/person-docs/search/live-search) | 25,204 | [titles.json](https://s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/fulldocs.crustdata.com/examples/people-search/linkedin_titles.json) |
| `REGION` | [Person Live Search](/person-docs/search/live-search) | 58,221 | [regions.json](https://s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/fulldocs.crustdata.com/examples/people-search/static-region-filter-values.json) |
| Employer industry | both (`INDUSTRY` live / `company_industries` indexed) | 433 | [industries.json](https://s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/fulldocs.crustdata.com/examples/people-search/static-linkedin-industries.json) |

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Indexed vs live.** `skills` is filterable on the indexed
> [Person Search](/person-docs/search/introduction). `CURRENT_TITLE` and
> `REGION` are filter fields on the real-time
> [Person Live Search](/person-docs/search/live-search) (the uppercase,
> real-time filter fields). On indexed Person Search, titles are matched as **text**
> with the `(.)` operator rather than chosen from this list.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Industries** are shared with company search — the same 433-value taxonomy
> applies to the employer-industry filters on both sides.

## What to do next

* **Discover values interactively** — [Person Autocomplete](/person-docs/autocomplete/introduction)
* **Build a search** — [Person Search](/person-docs/search/introduction)
* **Company values** — [Company filter values](/company-docs/filter-values)


# Person Identify API
Source: https://docs.crustdata.com/person-docs/identify/introduction

Resolve profile URLs, emails, or Google Scholar profile URLs to the people behind them: up to 25 in one synchronous call, or up to 300 emails as an async job.

## Endpoint essentials

| Detail | Value |
| - | - |
| **API key and headers** | Send `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY` and `x-api-version: 2025-11-01` with every request. |
| **Access** | Enabled per account on request. Check your account with [Permissions](/general/permissions). |
| **Free account** | No |
| **Credit cost** | 1 credit per identifier that resolves to a person, on both endpoints. Unmatched identifiers are free |
| **Batch size** | 25 per request on `/person/identify`, 300 per job on `/batch/person/identify` |
| **Rate limit** | `/person/identify`: 30 requests per minute. Batch: up to 5 jobs can run at the same time. |

**Use this when** you have an identifier and need to know *who* it belongs to.
Each match returns the person's `crustdata_person_id`, basic profile, and
profile URL. You pay only for identifiers that resolve to a person.

Two endpoints share the same result row:

| Endpoint | Identifiers per call | Accepts | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| `POST /person/identify` | 25 | `professional_network_profile_urls`, `emails`, `research_profile_urls` | Results in the same request |
| `POST /batch/person/identify` | 300 | `emails`, `business_emails`, `professional_network_profile_urls` | A job with a results file |

> [!NOTE]
>
> Identify is enabled per account. If your plan does not include it, contact
> your Crustdata account team.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Identify vs Enrich.** Identify answers *"who is this?"*. It returns the
> matched person's `crustdata_person_id`, `basic_profile` (name, headline,
> title, location), and `social_handles` (profile URL). If you also need
> contact data, full employment history, or company IDs per role, use
> [Person Enrich](/person-docs/enrichment/introduction) with the profile URL
> from the match.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Replace `YOUR_API_KEY` in each example with your actual API key. All requests
> require the `x-api-version: 2025-11-01` header.

## Identify a few people now

```
POST https://api.crustdata.com/person/identify
```

Send exactly one identifier key with up to 25 values. The response comes back
in the same request, one row per identifier, in the order you sent them.
Profile URLs and Scholar profile URLs match exactly. An email
matches exactly when the address is on file; otherwise Crustdata can match it
by the name in the address at the company that owns the domain, then by a
contact vendor lookup.

**Pricing:** 1 credit per identifier that resolves to a person.
Unmatched and redacted identifiers are never charged. See [Pricing](/general/pricing).&#xA;**&#x20;Limits:** up to 25 identifiers per request, 30 requests per
minute by default. See [Rate limits](/general/rate-limits).

### Request

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| `professional_network_profile_urls` | string\[] | One identifier of | Profile URLs to resolve. 1 credit per match. Result rows carry `match_type: "professional_network_profile_url"`. |
| `emails` | string\[] | One identifier of | Email addresses, business or personal. 1 credit per match. Result rows carry `match_type: "email"`. |
| `research_profile_urls` | string\[] | One identifier of | Google Scholar profile URLs, for example `https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=VGjeKSMAAAAJ`. Only Google Scholar is supported. 1 credit per match. Result rows carry `match_type: "research_profile_url"`. |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `business_emails` is not accepted here. Send business addresses in
> `emails`. An address that is not on file is matched by the name in the
> address at the company that owns the domain, when that match is confident
> enough for the company's size, and otherwise looked up with a contact
> vendor inside the same request. A match on a new address can take a few
> seconds longer than one already on file.

```bash Request theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.crustdata.com/person/identify \
  --header 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01' \
  --data '{
    "emails": [
      "abhilash@crustdata.com",
      "nobody@unknown-domain.com"
    ]
  }'
```

```json Response theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
[
  {
    "matched_on": "abhilash@crustdata.com",
    "match_type": "email",
    "match_status": "matched",
    "matches": [
      {
        "confidence_score": 1.0,
        "person_data": {
          "crustdata_person_id": 1068035,
          "basic_profile": {
            "name": "Abhilash Chowdhary",
            "headline": "Co-founder at Crustdata (YC F24) | Infra for building AI employees",
            "current_title": "Co-Founder & CEO",
            "summary": "Love building things. A software engineer with vast experience in shipping products spanning robotics, web technologies and quantitative finance.",
            "languages": ["English", "Hindi"],
            "location": {
              "city": "San Francisco",
              "state": "California",
              "country": "United States",
              "continent": "North America",
              "raw": "San Francisco, California, United States",
              "full_location": null
            }
          },
          "social_handles": {
            "professional_network_identifier": {
              "profile_url": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhilashchowdhary"
            },
            "dev_platform_identifier": { "profile_url": null },
            "twitter_identifier": { "slug": "" }
          },
          "updated_at": "2026-09-30T11:06:14.480375Z"
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "matched_on": "nobody@unknown-domain.com",
    "match_type": "email",
    "match_status": "not_found",
    "matches": []
  }
]
```

The example leaves some `basic_profile` fields out. A match returns the same
`basic_profile` fields, from the same source, that the
[Person Enrich reference](/person-docs/enrichment/reference#person_data-sections)
lists. Pass `social_handles.professional_network_identifier.profile_url` to
[Person Enrich](/person-docs/enrichment/introduction) for the full profile, or
to [Contact Enrich](/person-docs/contact/enrich) for emails and phone numbers.

### Response

A top-level array with one row per identifier you sent, in request order.

| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| `matched_on` | The identifier as you sent it. |
| `match_type` | The request key, singular: `professional_network_profile_url`, `email`, or `research_profile_url`. |
| `match_status` | `matched`, `not_found`, or `redacted`. See below. |
| `matches` | Zero or one match. |
| `matches[].confidence_score` | `1.0` for an exact match. An email matched by name and company domain carries the match score, `0.5` to `1.0`; the minimum rises with the company's headcount. |
| `matches[].person_data` | `crustdata_person_id`, `basic_profile`, `social_handles`, and `updated_at` for the matched person. |
| `matches[].person_data.social_handles` | The person's profile URL in `professional_network_identifier.profile_url`, plus `dev_platform_identifier.profile_url` and `twitter_identifier.slug`, which can be `null` or empty. |

| `match_status` | Meaning | Billed |
| - | - | - |
| `matched` | One person matched this identifier. | 1 credit |
| `not_found` | No person in Crustdata for this identifier. `matches` is empty. | No |
| `redacted` | The person asked Crustdata to remove their data and the request was approved. `matches` is empty, and the row does not change on retry. | No |

### Error responses

An invalid request body returns `400` with `error.type` of `invalid_request`
and one of these messages:

| `error.message` | When |
| - | - |
| `Exactly one identifier must be provided: professional_network_profile_urls, emails, crustdata_person_ids, or research_profile_urls` | The body has no identifier key. |
| `Only one identifier type can be provided. Found: emails, research_profile_urls` | The body has more than one identifier key. |
| `business_emails is not accepted by /person/identify. Use emails.` | The body uses `business_emails`. |
| `Maximum 25 values allowed for emails. Found 26` | The list has more than 25 values. |
| `Invalid emails: not-an-email, jane@example.com` | An email is malformed. The message lists each bad address. |
| `Invalid LinkedIn profile URLs: https://example.com/jane` | A profile URL is malformed. The message lists each bad URL. |
| `Invalid research profile URLs (only Google Scholar profile URLs with a `user` parameter are supported): https://example.com/jane` | A research profile URL is not a Google Scholar profile URL with a `user` parameter. |

```json 400 - business_emails theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "error": {
        "type": "invalid_request",
        "message": "business_emails is not accepted by /person/identify. Use emails.",
        "metadata": []
    }
}
```

If Identify is not enabled on your account, the request returns `403`:

```json 403 - not enabled theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "error": {
        "type": "permission_error",
        "message": "You do not have permission to access /person/identify.",
        "metadata": []
    }
}
```

When the identification service cannot answer, the request returns `503`.
Nothing is charged. Retry after a short wait.

```json 503 - service unavailable theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "error": {
        "type": "service_unavailable",
        "message": "Person identification is temporarily unavailable; retry shortly.",
        "metadata": [{ "retryable": true }]
    }
}
```

### Summary

| Detail | Value |
| - | - |
| **Endpoint** | `POST /person/identify` |
| **Auth** | Bearer token + `x-api-version: 2025-11-01` |
| **Request** | One of `professional_network_profile_urls`, `emails`, or `research_profile_urls` (max 25). |
| **Response** | Array, one row per identifier in request order: `matched_on`, `match_type`, `match_status`, `matches` (0 or 1). |
| **Billing** | 1 credit per matched identifier; unmatched and redacted free. |
| **Errors** | `400`, `401`, `402`, `403`, `429`, `500`, `503` |

***

## Identify a list in bulk

```
POST https://api.crustdata.com/batch/person/identify
```

For lists larger than 25, submit a job. It accepts `emails`,
`business_emails`, or `professional_network_profile_urls` (up to 300) and
delivers one record per identifier as a file. Batch rows carry `matched_on`,
`match_type`, and `matches` like the synchronous endpoint, and `match_type`
can also be `business_email`. Batch matches include
`social_handles.professional_network_identifier.urn_url`, the permanent form
of the profile URL.

### How it works

Reverse identify is an **asynchronous, two-call flow** — you submit a job, then
fetch the results once it finishes:

**1. Submit your emails**

`POST /batch/person/identify` with your list of `emails` (or
`professional_network_profile_urls`). You get a `batch_id` back
immediately.

**2. Poll, or wait for a webhook**

`GET /batch/{batch_id}` to check the job status — or pass a `webhook_url`
on submit and we call you when it finishes.

**3. Download the results**

Once `status` is `completed`, the status response includes a
`download_url`: a gzipped JSONL file with one record per input, valid for
5 days.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Emails already known to Crustdata resolve in seconds. Emails that require
> real-time retrieval take longer, which is why this endpoint is asynchronous.

**Pricing:** 1 credit per email that resolves to a person —
unmatched emails are free. See [Pricing](/general/pricing) for details.&#xA;**&#x20;Limits:** up to 300 identifiers per submission. Active jobs
are capped per account across the live endpoints (5 on default limits) - see
[Rate limits](/general/rate-limits#batch-job-concurrency).

***

### 1. Submit your emails

Send your emails in `emails` — business or personal addresses both work. The
response returns a `batch_id` immediately — the job runs asynchronously.

```bash Request theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.crustdata.com/batch/person/identify \
  --header 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01' \
  --data '{
    "emails": [
      "abhilash@crustdata.com",
      "ankit.harbhajanka@aequs.com"
    ]
  }'
```

```json Response theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "batch_id": "f0d86a5d-0031-4ca4-b350-92162fb38850",
    "status": "pending",
    "entity": "person",
    "action": "identify",
    "identifier_count": 2,
    "entities_requested": 2,
    "status_url": "/batch/f0d86a5d-0031-4ca4-b350-92162fb38850"
}
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> You can submit `professional_network_profile_urls` instead of
> `emails` to resolve profile URLs to their `crustdata_person_id`.
> Submit exactly one identifier type per job. To be notified when the job
> finishes instead of polling, include a `webhook_url` in the request body.

### 2. Get the results

Poll the `status_url` (or `GET /batch/{batch_id}`). While the job runs, `status`
is `pending` or `processing`. When it is `completed`, the response includes a
`download_url`.

```bash Request theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.crustdata.com/batch/f0d86a5d-0031-4ca4-b350-92162fb38850 \
  --header 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
  --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01'
```

```json Response theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "batch_id": "f0d86a5d-0031-4ca4-b350-92162fb38850",
    "status": "completed",
    "entity": "person",
    "action": "identify",
    "identifier_count": 2,
    "result_count": 2,
    "entities_requested": 2,
    "entities_fulfilled": 2,
    "created_at": "2026-10-01T08:07:32.927392+00:00",
    "completed_at": "2026-10-01T08:07:33.582570+00:00",
    "download_url": "https://crustdata-batch-api-data.s3.amazonaws.com/f0d86a5d-0031-4ca4-b350-92162fb38850/output/results.jsonl.gz?...",
    "download_urls": [
        "https://crustdata-batch-api-data.s3.amazonaws.com/f0d86a5d-0031-4ca4-b350-92162fb38850/output/part-000.jsonl.gz?..."
    ]
}
```

The `download_url` points to gzipped JSONL (`.jsonl.gz`) with one record per
submitted identifier. The link is valid for 5 days. `download_urls` lists the
same data split into parts. Both links are pre-signed, and the example trims
their query string to `?...`.

### Result format

Each line is one record for an input identifier:

```json theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
  "matched_on": "abhilash@crustdata.com",
  "match_type": "email",
  "matches": [
    {
      "confidence_score": 1.0,
      "person_data": {
        "crustdata_person_id": 1068035,
        "basic_profile": {
          "name": "Abhilash Chowdhary",
          "headline": "Co-founder at Crustdata (YC F24) | Infra for building AI employees",
          "current_title": "Co-Founder & CEO",
          "summary": "Love building things. A software engineer with vast experience in shipping products spanning robotics, web technologies and quantitative finance.",
          "languages": ["English", "Hindi"],
          "location": {
            "city": "San Francisco",
            "state": "California",
            "country": "United States",
            "continent": "North America",
            "raw": "San Francisco, California, United States",
            "full_location": null
          }
        },
        "social_handles": {
          "professional_network_identifier": {
            "profile_url": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhilashchowdhary",
            "urn_url": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/ACoAAAxLzxABgXUODmAZY4ZFYAxenZ10K0hTyY4"
          },
          "dev_platform_identifier": { "profile_url": null },
          "twitter_identifier": { "slug": "" }
        },
        "updated_at": "2026-09-30T11:06:14.480375Z"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

A match carries the person's profile URL in
`social_handles.professional_network_identifier.profile_url`. Submit that URL
to [Person Enrich](/person-docs/enrichment/introduction) for the full profile,
or to [Batch Contact Enrich](/person-docs/contact/batch) for emails and phone
numbers.

The same object holds `urn_url`, the permanent form of the profile URL. The
`profile_url` can change when the person edits it. The `urn_url` does not
change, so you can use it as a stable key for the person.

The example leaves some `basic_profile` fields out. A match returns the same
`basic_profile` fields that the
[Person Enrich reference](/person-docs/enrichment/reference#person_data-sections)
lists.

An email with no match returns an empty `matches` array (and is not billed):

```json theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{ "matched_on": "nobody@unknown-domain.com", "match_type": "email", "matches": [] }
```

#### Invalid emails

An invalid email does not fail the job. Its row has an empty `matches` array
and an `error_message` that gives the reason:

```json theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{ "matched_on": "not-an-email", "match_type": "email", "matches": [], "error_message": "Invalid email: malformed address" }
```

| `error_message` | When |
| - | - |
| `Invalid email: malformed address` | The address is not valid email syntax, for example it has no `@`. |
| `Invalid email: contains whitespace` | The address contains a space. |
| `Invalid email: non-ASCII characters` | The address contains a non-ASCII character, such as `é`. |
| `Invalid email: placeholder domain` | The domain is a placeholder, such as `example.com`. |
| `Invalid email: unrecognized domain` | The domain does not end in a known suffix. |

You do not pay for an invalid email, and the job's `result_count` leaves it
out. If every email in the request is invalid, the submit returns `400`
instead. See [Errors](#errors).

#### Personal emails resolve too

Reverse lookup is not limited to business addresses — a personal email (for
example a Gmail address) resolves the same way when it can be matched to a
person. Submit it in `emails` like any other address:

```bash theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.crustdata.com/batch/person/identify \
  --header 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01' \
  --data '{
    "emails": ["jane.doe91@gmail.com"]
  }'
```

The result row has the same shape as above. Personal addresses that cannot be
matched return the usual empty `matches` array and are not billed.

### Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| `emails` | string\[] | One identifier of | Emails to reverse-lookup — business or personal addresses. Max 300 per submission. Result rows carry `match_type: "email"`. |
| `business_emails` | string\[] | One identifier of | Emails to reverse-lookup, the same way as `emails`. Business and personal addresses both resolve. Max 300 per submission. Result rows carry `match_type: "business_email"`. |
| `professional_network_profile_urls` | string\[] | One identifier of | Profile URLs to resolve to a `crustdata_person_id`. Max 300 per submission. |
| `webhook_url` | string | No | URL to call when the job finishes, instead of polling. |

> [!NOTE]
>
> Submit exactly one identifier type per job: `emails`, `business_emails`, or
> `professional_network_profile_urls`. This endpoint does not accept `fields`.
> Every match returns the same sections.

### Response fields

| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| `matched_on` | The input value this record resolved (the email or profile URL you submitted). |
| `match_type` | `email`, `business_email`, or `professional_network_profile_url`. It mirrors the identifier key you submitted. |
| `matches` | Array of matches. Empty when nothing resolved. |
| `matches[].confidence_score` | Match confidence, `0`–`1`. |
| `matches[].person_data` | `crustdata_person_id`, `basic_profile`, `social_handles`, and `updated_at` for the matched person. |
| `matches[].person_data.social_handles` | The person's profile URL, in `professional_network_identifier.profile_url`, and its permanent form, in `professional_network_identifier.urn_url`. It also holds `dev_platform_identifier.profile_url` and `twitter_identifier.slug`, which can be `null` or empty. |
| `error_message` | Present only on a row whose email is invalid. See [Invalid emails](#invalid-emails). |

### Job lifecycle

| Status | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `pending` | Job accepted, not yet started. |
| `processing` | Job is running. |
| `completed` | Job finished — `download_url` is available. |
| `failed` | Job failed. Nothing was billed. |

### Errors

An invalid request body returns `400` with `error.type` of `invalid_request`
and one of these messages:

| `error.message` | When |
| - | - |
| `Exactly one identifier must be provided: emails, professional_network_profile_urls, or business_emails` | The body has no identifier. |
| `Only one identifier type can be provided. Found: emails, professional_network_profile_urls` | The body has more than one identifier type. |
| `Maximum 300 identifiers allowed for person/identify. Found 301` | The list has more than 300 values. |
| `'fields' is not a valid parameter.` | The body includes `fields`. |
| `Invalid emails: not-an-email, jane@example.com` | Every email in the list is invalid. The message lists them. |
| `Invalid professional_network_profile_urls: https://example.com/jane` | A profile URL is malformed. The message lists each bad URL. |

```json 400 - no identifier theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "error": {
        "type": "invalid_request",
        "message": "Exactly one identifier must be provided: emails, professional_network_profile_urls, or business_emails",
        "metadata": []
    }
}
```

The API rejects the whole request when one profile URL is malformed. It accepts
a request where only some emails are invalid. See
[Invalid emails](#invalid-emails).

If Identify is not enabled on your account, the submit returns `403` with
`error.type` of `permission_error`.

***

### API reference summary

| Detail | Value |
| - | - |
| **Submit** | `POST /batch/person/identify` |
| **Poll** | `GET /batch/{batch_id}` |
| **Auth** | Bearer token + `x-api-version: 2025-11-01` |
| **Request** | One of `emails`, `business_emails`, or `professional_network_profile_urls` (max 300). Optional: `webhook_url`. |
| **Response** | Submit returns `batch_id` + `status`; poll returns `status` and a `download_url` when complete. |
| **Output** | Gzipped JSONL, one record per identifier, download link valid 5 days. |
| **Billing** | 1 credit per matched person; unmatched identifiers are free. |
| **Errors** | `400`, `401`, `402`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500` |

For credit pricing, see [Pricing](/general/pricing). For throughput guidance, see
[Rate limits](/general/rate-limits).

## What to do next

* **Need contact data?** Use [Contact Enrich](/person-docs/contact/enrich).
* **Need full employment history?** Use [Person Enrich](/person-docs/enrichment/introduction) with the `profile_url` from the match.
* **Enrich contact info in bulk** — [Batch Contact Enrich](/person-docs/contact/batch) returns emails and phone numbers for a list of profile URLs.
* **Find people first** — use [Person Search](/person-docs/search/introduction) to build the list to identify.


# Batch People Search API
Source: https://docs.crustdata.com/person-docs/search/batch-search

Run one person search query asynchronously and receive the whole result set as a single file — from the indexed database (up to 10,000 records) or retrieved from the web in real time (up to 1,000 records).

## Endpoint essentials

| Detail | Value |
| - | - |
| **API key and headers** | Send `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY` and `x-api-version: 2025-11-01` with every request. |
| **Access** | Enterprise plans. Live batch is an add-on. Check your account with [Permissions](/general/permissions). |
| **Free account** | No |
| **Credit cost** | Same as People Search: 0.03 credits per result plus [premium groups](/general/pricing#premium-fields-in-search). Live batch is 2 credits per profile |
| **Batch size** | 10,000 results per job (1,000 for live) |
| **Rate limit** | Up to 5 jobs can run at the same time. |

Batch search runs one query asynchronously and delivers the **entire result
set** as a single file. Where [Person Search](/person-docs/search/introduction)
returns one cursor page per call, a batch job walks every page for you.

This page covers two batch endpoints:

* [**Batch search**](#batch-search) — results served from the indexed database, with higher caps and faster turnaround.
* [**Batch live search**](#batch-live-search) — results retrieved from the web in real time, fresher but with lower caps and slower.

<Snippet />

<Snippet />

***

## Batch search

```
POST https://api.crustdata.com/batch/person/search
```

Batch search runs one query asynchronously and delivers the **entire result
set** as a single file. Where [Person Search](/person-docs/search/introduction)
returns one cursor page per call, a batch job walks every page for you.

For fresher results retrieved from the web in real time, see
[Batch live search](#batch-live-search) below.

### How batch search differs from non-batch search

* **One query, whole result set.** You submit a single query; the job paginates server-side until `max_results` is reached or the matches run out.
* **`max_results` is the only volume control.** It clamps to **10,000** and defaults to that cap when omitted. Values above the cap are silently clamped; zero or negative values return `400`. The non-batch paging knobs — `limit`, `page`, `preview` — are silently ignored.
* **Flat records.** Each line in the results file has exactly the non-batch search record shape. No envelope.
* **Exact field projection.** When you pass `fields`, each record contains exactly those fields — nothing more. Omit `fields` to get every field your account can read.

### Database batch search

`POST /batch/person/search` takes the same filter fields and operators as
[Person Search](/person-docs/search/reference), with one extra rule: the top
level of `filters` **must** be an `{op, conditions}` group — a bare
`{field, type, value}` condition is rejected with `400`.

```bash Request theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.crustdata.com/batch/person/search \
  --header 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01' \
  --data '{
    "filters": {
      "op": "and",
      "conditions": [
        {"field": "experience.employment_details.current.title", "type": "(.)", "value": "engineer"}
      ]
    },
    "max_results": 2,
    "fields": ["basic_profile.name", "basic_profile.current_title"]
  }'
```

```json Response theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "batch_id": "a9afc353-8876-4e64-8b84-02a599561021",
    "status": "pending",
    "entity": "person",
    "action": "search",
    "identifier_count": 1,
    "entities_requested": 1,
    "status_url": "/batch/a9afc353-8876-4e64-8b84-02a599561021"
}
```

Search jobs always report `identifier_count: 1` — the one query. When the job
completes, the downloaded file contains flat records with exactly the
requested fields:

```json The results file (all records) theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{"basic_profile": {"current_title": "Principal Software Engineer", "name": "Man Sum Simon Yuen"}}
{"basic_profile": {"current_title": "Knowledge Systems Architect · Context Engineer", "name": "Emily Anderson"}}
```

#### Nest groups for or-logic

Groups nest inside `conditions`. This finds engineers in either the United
States or Canada:

```bash Request theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.crustdata.com/batch/person/search \
  --header 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01' \
  --data '{
    "filters": {
      "op": "and",
      "conditions": [
        {"field": "experience.employment_details.current.title", "type": "(.)", "value": "engineer"},
        {
          "op": "or",
          "conditions": [
            {"field": "basic_profile.location.country", "type": "=", "value": "United States"},
            {"field": "basic_profile.location.country", "type": "=", "value": "Canada"}
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "max_results": 2,
    "fields": ["basic_profile.name", "basic_profile.location.country"]
  }'
```

```json The results file (all records) theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{"basic_profile": {"location": {"country": "United States"}, "name": "Emily Anderson"}}
{"basic_profile": {"location": {"country": "United States"}, "name": "Michael Phillips"}}
```

> [!TIP]
>
> Exact-match values must match the **indexed** value — both `"United States"`
> and `"United States of America"` exist as `basic_profile.location.country`
> values. Use an `or` group or [Person
> Autocomplete](/person-docs/autocomplete/introduction) to discover indexed
> values first.

#### Two warnings before you submit large jobs

> [!WARNING]
>
> Unknown filter field names are **not rejected at submit time** the way
> non-batch search rejects them — a typo in `field` simply produces a job that
> completes with 0 results. Double-check field names against the [search
> reference](/person-docs/search/reference) first.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Do not pass a non-empty `sorts` array — the job will complete with **0
> results**. Sort the downloaded file instead, for example `jq -s
>       'sort_by(.basic_profile.name) | .[]' results.jsonl`.

### Errors

```json 400 — no filters theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "error": {
        "type": "invalid_request",
        "message": "`filters` must be provided for search",
        "metadata": []
    }
}
```

```json 400 — bare condition instead of a group theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "error": {
        "type": "invalid_request",
        "message": "Invalid filter shape: [{'type': 'missing', 'loc': ('op',), 'msg': 'Field required', ...}]",
        "metadata": []
    }
}
```

***

## Batch live search

> [!NOTE]
>
> Batch live search is available to accounts with the `live` entitlement. The
> [Batch search](#batch-search) endpoint above is generally available.

```
POST https://api.crustdata.com/batch/person/professional_network/search/live
```

Batch live search runs one query asynchronously and delivers the **entire
result set** as a single file, with results retrieved from the web in real
time. Where [Person Live Search](/person-docs/search/live-search) returns one
cursor page per call, a batch job walks every page for you.

For results served from the indexed database — higher caps and faster — see
[Batch search](#batch-search) above.

### How batch live search differs from non-batch search

* **One query, whole result set.** You submit a single query; the job paginates server-side until `max_results` is reached or the matches run out.
* **`max_results` is the only volume control.** It clamps to **1,000** and defaults to that cap when omitted. Values above the cap are silently clamped; zero or negative values return `400`. The non-batch paging knobs — `limit`, `page`, `preview` — are silently ignored.
* **Flat records.** Each line in the results file has exactly the non-batch search record shape. No envelope.
* **Exact field projection.** When you pass `fields`, each record contains exactly those fields — nothing more. Omit `fields` to get every field your account can read.

### Live batch search

`POST /batch/person/professional_network/search/live` retrieves results from
the web in real time — fresher than the database, capped at **1,000** records
per job, fetched internally in pages of 25, and slower. Live jobs are the most
likely to end `failed` with an `error_message`.

Live filters use a **flat list** of `{field, type, value}` objects — not the
`{op, conditions}` group — and `field` takes an uppercase filter type instead
of a dotted path:

```bash Request theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.crustdata.com/batch/person/professional_network/search/live \
  --header 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01' \
  --data '{
    "filters": [
      {"field": "CURRENT_TITLE", "type": "in", "value": ["Software Engineer"]},
      {"field": "REGION", "type": "in", "value": ["United States"]}
    ],
    "max_results": 2,
    "fields": ["basic_profile.name", "basic_profile.headline"]
  }'
```

```json Response theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "batch_id": "65de822c-f7d3-4b4c-af89-ef683704889e",
    "status": "pending",
    "entity": "person",
    "action": "search_live",
    "identifier_count": 1,
    "entities_requested": 1,
    "status_url": "/batch/65de822c-f7d3-4b4c-af89-ef683704889e"
}
```

```json The results file (all records) theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{"basic_profile": {"headline": "Full-Stack Software Developer | Spring Boot | Angular | MySQL | Java | TypeScript | US Citizen", "name": "Sael Torres - Diaz"}}
{"basic_profile": {"headline": "Software Engineer - Frontend / Backend / TypeScript / JavaScript / React / Nest.js / Angular / Spring. Authorized to work in the USA without a current/future sponsorship.", "name": "Daniel Ignatyev"}}
```

Valid filter types: `CURRENT_COMPANY`, `PAST_COMPANY`, `CURRENT_TITLE`,
`PAST_TITLE`, `SCHOOL`, `COMPANY_HEADQUARTERS`, `COMPANY_HEADCOUNT`,
`COMPANY_TYPE`, `FUNCTION`, `INDUSTRY`, `NUM_OF_FOLLOWERS`, `REGION`,
`SENIORITY_LEVEL`, `YEARS_AT_CURRENT_COMPANY`, `YEARS_IN_CURRENT_POSITION`,
`YEARS_OF_EXPERIENCE`, `FOLLOWER_OF`, `CONNECTION_OF`, `KEYWORD`,
`FIRST_NAME`, `LAST_NAME`,
`NETWORK_DEGREE`, `PROFILE_LANGUAGE`, `SERVICE_CATEGORY`, `CONTACT_INTEREST` —
the same filters as the non-batch
[Person Live Search](/person-docs/search/live-search), which documents
per-filter value formats. An unknown filter type returns `400` listing the
valid values.

`filters` is required. Omitting it returns `400`.

### Errors

```json 400 — group instead of a flat list theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "error": {
        "type": "invalid_request",
        "message": "`filters` for live search must be a list of {field, type, value} objects",
        "metadata": []
    }
}
```
